headline: The phone now teaches the clap until you learn it
lede: Every human recording in the PLAICRAFT store heard zero claps, so the ±50 ms audio-alignment proof could never close — and the old once-per-device coach pill burned its lesson on exactly the players who missed it. The coach now re-asks every take until the habit lands, and retires the moment the mic hears a clap.

notes.text: Device state goes none → shown → learned: a take whose live mic hears a clap marks the device learned forever; a mic-live take that ends silent brings the pill back next take. Jon's phone, which consumed the old pill testing the last build, sees it again on its next consented take.

The watch is the recorder's own analyser tap — frames of mic level, clapSync's onset law in frame units, take bytes untouched. Its bias is one-sided by design: a missed clap costs a 5-second pill, never a lost proof.

Proven end-to-end in a browser that never clapped: pill paints at green REC, silent slaps end the take honestly red, the flag clears, and a fresh boot repaints the pill. recordcheck 222/222 with the demotion rule mutant killed at exactly its pin; the off-tempo suite flake was fingerprinted against origin/main on the same loaded box, not excused.

S1's last open line is now one physical act: consent YES+YES on the phone, three sharp claps with your first taps. When a clap-carrying take uploads, the lane's own grade command posts the ±50 ms verdict and the acceptance list closes on evidence.
